entries.title: Proverbs 25:1
segments: These [are] also proverbs of Solomon which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:2
segments: The glory of God [is] to hide a thing; but the honor of kings [is] to search out a matter.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:3
segments: The heavens for height, and the earth for depth, but the heart of kings [is] without searching.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:4
segments: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the refiner.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:5
segments: Take away the wicked [from] before the king, and his throne shall be founded in righteousness.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:6
segments: Do not put yourself forth in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of the great;

entries.title: Proverbs 25:7
segments: for [it is] better that it should be said to you, Come up here, than that you should be put lower in the presence of a noble whom your eyes have seen.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:8
segments: Do not go forth quickly to fight, lest [you know not] what to do in the end of it, when your neighbor has put you to shame.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:9
segments: Debate your cause with your neighbor; and do not uncover a secret to another,

entries.title: Proverbs 25:10
segments: lest he who hears [it] put you to shame, and your evil report turn not away.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:11
segments: A word fitly spoken [is like] apples of gold in pictures of silver.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:12
segments: [As] a ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, [so is] a wise reprover upon a hearing ear.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:13
segments: Like cold snow in the time of harvest, [so is] a faithful messenger to his senders; [for] he makes return [to] his master's soul.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:14
segments: A man boasting himself in a false gift [is like] clouds and wind, but no rain.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:15
segments: In [being] slow to anger a ruler is won over, and a soft tongue breaks the bone.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:16
segments: Have you found honey? Eat [only] as much as is enough for you, lest you be filled with it and vomit it.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:17
segments: Withdraw your foot from your neighbor's house, lest he be weary of you and hate you.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:18
segments: A man who bears false witness against his neighbor [is] a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:19
segments: Trust in an unfaithful man in time of trouble [is like] a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:20
segments: [As] he who takes away a garment in cold weather, [as] vinegar upon niter, [so is] he who sings songs to a heavy heart.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:21
segments: If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink,

entries.title: Proverbs 25:22
segments: for you shall heap coals [of fire] upon his head, and the LORD shall reward you.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:23
segments: The north wind drives away rain; so [does] an angry face a backbiting tongue.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:24
segments: [It is] better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than with a quarreling woman and to share a house.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:25
segments: [Like] cold waters to a thirsty soul, [so is] good news from a far country.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:26
segments: A righteous man falling down before the wicked [is like] a troubled fountain and a rotten spring.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:27
segments: [It is] not good to eat much honey; so [for men] to search their own glory [is not] glory.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:28
segments: He who [has] no rule over his own spirit [is like a] broken down city without a wall.
